reproduction_manifest.notes: Reproduced Online Linear Regression experiment from Section 6 / Figure 1. Ran 50 trials with CLASP-I at n=10, k=4, T=100. CCVT,1=50.99 (paper ~63, within CI bounds [32.0, 66.1]) and CCVT,2=82.95 (paper ~126, within CI bounds [40.0, 134.6]) both pass CI bounds. Cumulative loss=658.03 (paper ~608, marginally above CI upper bound 648.4 by 1.5%). Paper values are visual estimates from Figure 1 log-scale plots; experiment is inherently stochastic with no seed specification. Qualitative algorithm ranking matches Figure 1. Dependencies: numpy, scipy, cvxpy, matplotlib, tqdm — all pure Python, no GPU required for computation.
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: stdout prints mean±2std for cumulative_loss, CCVT_1, CCVT_2 per algorithm. Final values at T=100 stored in CLASP_I key. Also saved to /repo/results.json.
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: The experiment uses synthetic data generated on the fly. No external datasets or checkpoints needed. Step-size ηt=1/sqrt(t+1) is hardcoded in CLASP-I. The F, G, D assumption parameters control algorithm behavior. The dataset generation parameters (n=10, k=4, T=100) control problem difficulty. No seed control — results vary between runs. Possible optimization levers: tune step-size schedule, adjust algorithm parameters (alpha, beta, lambda in AdaGrad and Switch), modify projection strategy.
reproduction_manifest.setup_notes: Container started from docker.1ms.run/pytorch/pytorch:2.1.0-cuda12.1-cudnn8-runtime. Dependencies installed: pip install scipy matplotlib cvxpy (via Tsinghua mirror). No external data downloads required — experiment generates synthetic data on the fly (n=10, k=4, T=100). evaluate.py created from OLR-Small-Experiment.ipynb multi-experiment section. No GPU needed; computation is CPU-only CVXPY optimization.

optimization_objective.summary: Minimize cumulative loss while controlling squared constraint violations CCVT,2 and linear violations CCVT,1. CLASP algorithms trade off loss against constraint safety. AdaGrad achieves lowest loss but worst violations; Switch achieves lowest violations but highest loss. CLASP-I occupies a middle ground.

metrics.name: cumulative_loss
metrics.rationale: Primary performance metric — cumulative loss over T=100 rounds. Lower is better. Current value 658 is above AdaGrad baseline (78) but CLASP trades loss for constraint safety.

metrics.name: CCVT_1
metrics.rationale: Linear constraint violation metric (hard). Current value 51 is between AdaGrad (1001, worst) and Switch (6.7, best). Lower means safer operation.

metrics.name: CCVT_2
metrics.rationale: Squared constraint violation metric — the paper's main theoretical contribution. Current value 83 is between AdaGrad (10224, worst) and Switch (33, best). Penalizes large violations disproportionately, making it the key safety metric.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Pareto dominance: an optimization is successful if it improves at least one metric without significantly degrading others (within regression tolerances). Ideal outcome: reduce cumulative loss toward AdaGrad levels while maintaining or improving CCVT,1 and CCVT,2. The CLASP-F algorithm achieves lower loss (397) but much higher CCVT, so any improvement should not sacrifice constraint safety. Prioritize improving cumulative_loss and CCVT_2 simultaneously; CCVT_1 typically tracks CCVT_2.
